bull.t: Rapid revenue growth and strong margins
bull.b: Astera Labs has reached meaningful scale while maintaining exceptional gross and net margins, indicating valuable connectivity products and operating leverage. If demand for AI and cloud infrastructure remains strong, this combination can support durable earnings growth and continued investment in its roadmap.

bull.t: Debt-free balance sheet and solid cash generation
bull.b: The debt-free balance sheet and substantial liquidity give Astera Labs flexibility to fund research, product ramps, and strategic expansion without depending on borrowing. Positive operating and free cash flow also provide internal funding capacity, strengthening resilience through investment cycles.

bull.t: Strong adoption of next-generation connectivity products
bull.b: Rapid PCIe 6 adoption and the early Scorpio X volume ramp show that Astera Labs is securing demand across evolving AI infrastructure architectures. Broader product adoption can increase content per system, diversify growth beyond existing products, and reinforce its role in high-bandwidth interconnects.

bear.b: Recent profitability is strong, but the prior multi-year loss period demonstrates that earnings have not yet been proven across a full operating cycle. This history raises the risk that margins and net income could be more sensitive to product transitions, demand changes, or execution than current results suggest.

bear.t: Free cash flow has declined and was previously inconsistent
bear.b: Although current cash generation is positive, the year-over-year decline and earlier periods of negative cash flow indicate that conversion can fluctuate materially. Continued investment and working-capital requirements may therefore absorb part of reported earnings, limiting the consistency of internally funded expansion.

bear.t: Scorpio ramp concentration and execution risk
bear.b: Scorpio is expected to become the largest product family, but its near-term contribution depends heavily on a limited number of major customer programs. Delayed deployments, slower qualification, or execution issues at those accounts could materially affect growth and make results less predictable while broader adoption develops.
